findings.status: Confirmed for released reproduction recipe and chosen-pair interpretation
findings.title: Gaussian recipe breaks claimed observational equivalence of CTF1 and CTF2
findings.claim: The chosen CTF1/CTF2 pair shares the observational law but has different counterfactuals; the higher CTF2 error suggests CausalNF learns CTF1.

evidence.detail: CTF1 has X2=U2 or U2-1;CTF2 has X2=U2 or -U2 by sign of X1; both X1=U1,X3=X2+U3.
Documented reproduction path selects dataset.base_version1, independent standard Normal noises. Configuration and sampler path traced statically.
On X1<0, probability1/2, CTF1 X2~N(-1,1),CTF2 X2~N(0,1). Distinct conditional means imply distinct observational laws. CTF3/4 already differ on(X1,X2).
Stored robustness2 means/SDs for CTF1-4 round exactly to Tables3-4; parsed JSON only, no unpickling.

findings.dependency: Observational equivalence is the premise of the selected non-identifiability demonstration and the claim that the learner defaults to CTF1. The released experiment cannot substantiate that explanation.
findings.impact: Core chosen-pair experimental/interpretation chain invalid under supplied recipe; different score magnitudes alone do not identify a learned SCM.
counterevidence: Gaussian CTF2 remains observationally equivalent to distinct M0:X2=U2 and same other equations; broader non-identifiability may still hold.
Saved output associates recipe family with numbers but is not an execution receipt; historical overrides remain possible.
Reported larger errors need not be false, and broader evaluation agenda can remain.
findings.repair: Use a mathematically consistent noise/mechanism pair, disclose exact run configurations, and reevaluate the interpreted performance. Uniform U2 with U1 retaining both signs repairs CTF1/2 observational equality; additionally uniform U3 repairs corresponding CTF3/4 pair.
findings.repair_validation: Analytic conditional-law proof and counterfactual witness verified; no author experiment modified or rerun

findings.status: Confirmed statistical procedure and inference error
findings.title: Independent-samples Welch test compares all seed outcomes with an overlapping subset
findings.claim: One significant comparison among100realizations indicates realism checks rarely identify meaningfully lower ATE bias.

evidence.detail: Each passing error is present in both lists; ttest_ind(all_biases,filtered_biases,equal_var=False) treats the means as independent.
Pbar-Abar=(k/n)(Pbar-Fbar);conditional on fixed membership and independent disjoint outcomes, Var=(k/n)^2(sigmaP²/m+sigmaF²/k). Common-variance overlap covariance sigma²/n is omitted.
20nonnegative illustration values yield naive p0.1243025127 vs disjoint/covariance-aware p0.0084890857. Not authors' data or corrected significance count.
Non-rejection does not establish negligible practical effect. Tests with<2passing seeds skipped while denominator100retained; actual skipped count unknown.

findings.dependency: B.2 tests whether realism filtering addresses generator-error behavior underlying central RealCause critique.
findings.impact: Published significance count through this procedure cannot validate frequency-of-useful-filtering conclusion; reanalysis could change it.
counterevidence: Committed aggregates substantiate descriptive ATE variability.
No claim filter actually improves performance or actual corrected count differs.
Per-seed KS/error records missing; all-passing and skipped cases not reconstructed.
findings.repair: Define selection estimand; analyze disjoint groups with appropriate assumptions or resample complete seed/filter/error records; report effect sizes, uncertainty, practical threshold, acceptance rate and valid-test counts.
findings.repair_validation: Contrast derivation and illustrative arithmetic checked only; actual empirical repair pending raw records

findings.title: Mean Euclidean counterfactual error labeled RMSE

evidence.detail: Per-unit sqrt(sum_j e_ij²), then arithmetic mean over units and counterfactual queries; no later squared aggregation.
For scalar errors0and2, mean norm1differs from vector RMSEsqrt2; coordinate normalization is a separate convention.

findings.impact: Metric must be explicitly renamed/defined or recomputed; no observed ranking reversal or falsified high-error trend
counterevidence: Mean Euclidean error is a legitimate metric if named accurately.
Stored rounded CTF outputs agree with tables; exact historical override limits retained.
findings.repair: State precise mean-norm definition or recompute intended RMSE from per-unit predictions and update labels.
findings.repair_validation: Algebraic distinction and released aggregation trace verified; no recomputed performance
